title: ZXNet: ZX Calculus-Driven Graph Neural Network Framework for Quantum Circuit Equivalence Checking
problem: Quantum circuits require transpilation into hardware-compatible instructions, significantly altering designs; existing equivalence checking methods struggle with scalability and computational overhead.
motivation: Equivalence checking is essential for validating quantum circuit transpilation; high computational cost and poor scalability limit practical deployment.
method: ZXNet converts quantum circuits into simplified diagram representations using ZX calculus, a mathematical notation that expresses quantum operations as connected shapes. Machine learning models called graph neural networks then learn patterns in these diagrams to determine if two circuits are equivalent. This approach dramatically reduces the computational work needed to verify whether different circuit implementations perform the same function.
key_novelty: ZXNet combines mathematical representations of quantum circuits (ZX calculus) with machine learning models that learn patterns in connected data (graph neural networks) to verify circuit equivalence.
contributions: ZXNet framework combining ZX calculus with GNN-based learning
99.4% validation accuracy with 62x speedup over state-of-the-art
45.83% scalability improvement, 42.22% per-qubit verification time reduction, 5.94% accuracy gains
primary_theme: ZX calculus-driven GNN for quantum circuit verification
